name: Palmar approach to the proximal interphalangeal joint
aliases: volar Bruner approach to the PIP joint
shotgun approach to the PIP joint
corridor: Volar Bruner interval through the flexor sheath between the A2 and A4 pulleys, retracting the flexor tendons and detaching the volar plate to open the PIP joint

positioning.text: Position supine with the hand on a hand table under tourniquet control.

surface_landmarks.text: Use the palmar flexor skin creases as a guide, with the incision apex at the intermediate crease over the PIP joint.

incision.text: Make a carefully planned Bruner zig-zag palmar incision using the flexor creases.

superficial_interval.text: Elevate thin skin flaps and identify and gently mobilize the digital arteries and nerves on each side.

deep_interval.text: Incise the C1, A3, and C2 pulleys laterally near their bony attachments leaving a cuff for repair, preserve the A2 and A4 pulleys, retract the flexor tendons with a loop, and detach the volar plate as a flap.

layers.text: Skin, subcutaneous tissue with digital neurovascular bundles, flexor sheath and pulleys, flexor tendons, volar plate, and the PIP joint.

structures_at_risk.text: The digital arteries and nerves on each side, the vincular arteries to the flexor tendons, and the A2 and A4 pulleys are at risk.

danger_zones.text: The lateral borders of the sheath are the danger zones for the digital neurovascular bundles; cutting the A2 or A4 pulleys risks tendon bowstringing.

retraction_hazards.text: Retract the mobilized digital neurovascular bundles gently and preserve the vincular blood supply to the flexor tendons.

exposure.text: Opens the volar PIP joint fully, and dividing both collateral ligaments allows hyperextension (shotgun) exposure for comminuted fractures.

limitations.text: Preservation of the A2 and A4 pulleys constrains proximal and distal extension, and wide exposure requires collateral ligament release.

indications.text: Indicated for volar PIP fracture-dislocations and intra-articular fractures of the base of the middle phalanx.

closure.text: Repair the volar plate with pullout or anchor sutures and reattach the A3 and, where possible, the C1 and C2 pulleys with nonabsorbable monofilament.

complications.text: Complications include digital nerve injury, flexor tendon bowstringing from pulley loss, PIP stiffness, and skin flap problems.

procedure_applications.condition: A volar PIP fracture-dislocation or intra-articular base of middle phalanx fracture needs open joint access

What is the shotgun maneuver for PIP exposure?
questions.answer: Dividing both collateral ligaments to hyperextend and fully open the joint.
